story.title: Trump Pardons Turkeys Freedom and Feathers at White House Ceremony
story.summary: President Trump held the annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon ceremony at the White House, granting pardons to two turkeys named Freedom and Feathers. This tradition allows the birds to skip Thanksgiving dinner and continue living. The turkeys were introduced prior to the ceremony, where they were housed at a hotel in Washington.

explore_lenses.label: How were Freedom and Feathers selected?
explore_lenses.title: Public voting chose the names and on-stage bird
explore_lenses.summary: The two birds were raised specifically for the event, and the White House used public polls first to name them and then to select the turkey that would appear for the ceremonial moment.

claims.text: The White House said Americans chose the names Freedom and Feathers in an online poll; the birds were raised at Deans Gap Farm in West Virginia by Scott and Becky Rightsell.
A second public vote determined which bird would receive the White House's in-person ceremonial recognition, while both birds were designated to be pardoned.
Freedom, rather than Feathers, attended the November 24 White House event; AP reported that both birds received pardons.
Rightsell said temperament and appearance were key considerations in choosing birds able to handle cameras, noise and crowds, characterizing the assignment as a major honor for turkey farmers.

explore_lenses.label: What happens to the turkeys now?
explore_lenses.title: They are headed to retirement at Texas A&M
explore_lenses.summary: The ceremony does not place the birds into a government program; it transfers the public-facing part of the tradition into a university-hosted retirement arrangement.

claims.text: The White House said both Freedom and Feathers would live out their days at Texas A&M after the ceremony.
CBS reported that this would be the first retirement in Texas for National Thanksgiving turkeys and that Texas A&M had prepared a climate-controlled enclosure with outdoor access.
CBS reported that six Texas A&M undergraduate students were selected to oversee the birds' day-to-day care.
National Turkey Federation chairwoman Christy Puffenbarger said the turkeys could appear at Texas A&M's November 27 rivalry football game against the University of Texas.

explore_lenses.label: How old is the turkey-pardon tradition?
explore_lenses.title: The presentation dates to 1947; annual pardons to 1989
explore_lenses.summary: The event combines two related traditions: the turkey industry's White House presentation and the later annual use of a ceremonial presidential pardon.

claims.text: The White House described the 2026 event as the 79th National Thanksgiving Turkey presentation and said the National Turkey Federation's first presentation occurred in 1947.
The White House Historical Association says President George H. W. Bush's 1989 action made the turkey pardon an annual tradition, after earlier presidents had occasionally spared or reprieved birds.
The association characterizes the modern event as a lighthearted annual press occasion tied to the National Turkey Federation's presentation of birds to the White House.

story_report.summary: President Trump pardoned the turkeys Freedom and Feathers during the annual Thanksgiving ceremony at the White House. Freedom attended the Nov. 24 event, while both birds received pardons. The birds, raised at Deans Gap Farm in West Virginia, are set to live out their days at Texas A&M University rather than become Thanksgiving dinner. The White House said Americans selected their names through an online poll, and a separate vote chose the bird for in-person ceremonial recognition.

sections.heading: Texas A&M Prepares Turkey Retirement
sections.body: Texas A&M is to become the first Texas retirement home for National Thanksgiving turkeys, according to CBS. The university prepared a climate-controlled enclosure with outdoor access for Freedom and Feathers, and six undergraduate students were selected to manage their day-to-day care. The White House said both birds would spend the rest of their lives there.

sections.heading: Turkey Pardon Tradition Has Deep Roots
sections.body: The White House described the 2026 ceremony as the 79th National Thanksgiving Turkey presentation, a program whose first National Turkey Federation presentation took place in 1947. The White House Historical Association says presidents had occasionally spared or reprieved birds before George H. W. Bush made the pardon an annual tradition in 1989. It characterizes the modern event as a lighthearted annual press occasion linked to the federation's turkey presentation.

unresolved.text: National Turkey Federation Chairwoman Christy Puffenbarger said the birds could appear at Texas A&M's Nov. 27 rivalry football game against the University of Texas, but no appearance was confirmed.

related_stories.title: Melania Trump Unveils 2026 White House Christmas Tree
related_stories.summary: First Lady Melania Trump welcomed the official 2026 White House Christmas tree in a ceremony on November 23, 2026. The tree, an 18-foot fir from Silent Night Evergreens in Wisconsin, arrived in a horse-drawn carriage, marking the beginning of the festive season at the White House.

related_stories.title: Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni to Stand Trial for Witness Tampering
related_stories.summary: Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, Carla Bruni, are scheduled to face trial in 2027. They are facing allegations of criminal conspiracy and witness tampering related to illegal campaign funding from Libya during Sarkozy's 2007 election campaign. This follows Sarkozy's imprisonment last year for separate charges.

related_stories.title: Trump Awards Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump has awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani, the former mayor of New York City, recognizing his leadership during the 9/11 attacks. Giuliani, who has been a close ally of Trump and served as his personal lawyer, has faced controversy for his role in efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election results. The award ceremony took place in the Oval Office.
